keyVerseText: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old: close: Heb. hedge, or, wall
rootMeaning: The root of הֲרִיסָה (hărîyçâh) is הָרַס (hâraç), which conveys the action of breaking down, pulling down, or utterly destroying. This root emphasizes a forceful dismantling or overthrowing, suggesting not merely damage but a complete ruin or demolition. Thus, the noun form הֲרִיסָה captures the tangible result of this destructive process — a concrete ruin or something that has been thoroughly demolished, going beyond the general English idea of 'ruin' to imply a state of being broken apart or thrown down.
usageInScripture: The word הֲרִיסָה appears only once in the Hebrew Bible, specifically in Amos 9:11, where it is translated as 'his ruins.' This singular occurrence shows the term used concretely to refer to the physical remnants of something destroyed, in this case, the tabernacle or dwelling associated with David. The consistent translation as 'ruins' highlights its emphasis on the aftermath of destruction, the broken remains that stand as evidence of what was once whole. This focused usage underscores the word’s strong connection to tangible, visible destruction rather than metaphorical or abstract ruin.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding הֲרִיסָה enriches our grasp of biblical themes of judgment and restoration. The term’s original meaning of a complete demolition reminds us of the seriousness of sin and divine judgment that can bring about such ruin. Yet, its presence in a prophetic promise like Amos 9:11 also points to God’s power to raise up and restore what has been broken down. For the Christian faith, this word underscores the hope that God can rebuild and redeem even the most devastated circumstances, reflecting Christ’s work of restoration and renewal. It calls believers to trust in God’s sovereign ability to transform ruin into restoration, a foundational truth for living in hope amidst brokenness.
keyVerseReflection: Amos 9:11 declares, 'In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen... and I will raise up his ruins.' Here, הֲרִיסָה signifies the literal broken remains of the fallen tabernacle, emphasizing the completeness of its destruction. The promise to raise up these ruins conveys God’s commitment to restoration, transforming what was once demolished back to its former glory. This word deepens the verse’s message by highlighting the tangible reality of destruction that God will reverse, offering profound hope that no ruin is beyond His redeeming power.
